_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 11 Mathematics P2 (statistics, analytical geometry, trigonometry, measurement and Euclidean geometry), November 2025 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers transcribed from the rendered pages of the official PDFs
(paper2.pdf, paper2_memo.pdf); the text layer does not hold usable equations. Notation:
^ for powers, sqrt() for roots, a/b for fractions, decimal commas as printed. memo_answer is the
guideline's final answer and memo_working its working (tick marks and mark descriptors left out).
The guideline is bilingual (English/Afrikaans); only the English is transcribed. Graphs and diagrams are described
in brackets in the question text. The information sheet printed with the paper is not transcribed.
FORMAT: 150 marks, 3 hours, ten compulsory questions (Q1 11, Q2 10, Q3 27, Q4 32, Q5 10, Q6 7, Q7 11,
Q8 15, Q9 22, Q10 5). Geometry answers go in a separate ANSWER BOOK with the diagrams
(paper2_answer_book.pdf). Angle names use a circumflex on the vertex letter as printed (WÛQ, Ô1).

questions.memo_working: QP̂O = θ + α (SP̂O = θ [alt. ∠s, SP ∥ OT]); QÔP = β - θ; OQ̂P = 180° - (θ + α) - (β - θ) [sum of ∠s in Δ] = 180° - (β + α)

questions.context: QUESTION 8 | 8.1 In the diagram below, O is the centre of the circle. AC is a chord. OB is drawn perpendicular to the chord.
questions.text: Use the diagram above to prove the theorem which states that the line drawn from the centre of a circle perpendicular to a chord bisects the chord, that is, prove that AB = BC.
questions.topic: Euclidean geometry: circle theorems (centre, chords, angles)
questions.memo_answer: Construction: join OA and OC. In ΔAOB and ΔCOB: AO = CO [radii]; AB̂O = CB̂O = 90° [∠s on a str. line]; OB = OB [common]; ΔAOB ≡ ΔCOB [RHS]; therefore AB = BC.

questions.text: Prove that MNQP is a cyclic quadrilateral.
questions.topic: Euclidean geometry: cyclic quadrilaterals and tangents
questions.memo_answer: SP̂R = Q̂1 [tan chord theorem]; SP̂R = M̂1 [corresp. ∠s, MN ∥ PR]; therefore Q̂1 = M̂1; MNQP is a cyclic quad [converse ext. ∠ of a cyclic quad]
questions.memo_note: The guideline writes SP̂Q for the tangent-chord angle; the angle meant is SP̂R (between tangent PS and chord PR).

questions.text: Prove that PN bisects SP̂R
questions.topic: Euclidean geometry: cyclic quadrilaterals and tangents
questions.memo_answer: P̂3 = N̂2 [alt. ∠s, MN ∥ PR]; N̂2 = Q̂1 [∠s in same segment]; Q̂1 = P̂4 [tan chord theorem]; therefore P̂3 = P̂4, so PN bisects SP̂R
